minutes.headline: Finance Committee set its fall meeting calendar, discussed a project-review rubric, and heard a Turkey Hill cost illustration.
minutes.summary: The committee discussed file sharing, the special town meeting calendar, and a draft rubric for judging large building and capital projects. The finance director reported FY20 year-end results and a free cash estimate, and members discussed CARES Act funding, possible school IT upgrades, bus fees, and outsourcing. A member presented a Turkey Hill replacement cost illustration. The only vote was to adjourn.

what_happened.line: The Finance Committee set its next meetings for Sept 24, Oct 8 and Oct 15, with the warrant first reviewed Oct 8 and recommendations due Oct 15.
The finance director reported that FY20 revenues exceeded estimates, spending came in under budget, and free cash was expected to rise over last year's certified amount.
The committee discussed a draft rubric for judging large building and capital projects; two members were assigned to work on it.
A member presented a Turkey Hill replacement cost illustration, before state reimbursement; it is to be shared and attached to the minutes.
Members discussed possible school IT upgrades for hybrid learning, which one member hoped to fund outside the normal capital process.

why_it_matters: The free cash estimate and the fall warrant review shape what Town Meeting is asked to fund and how much of it falls on the tax bill.

The project-review rubric and the Turkey Hill cost illustration bear on how future large building projects are judged and what residents may later be asked to vote on, and funding school IT outside the capital process would change how that spending is reviewed.
